s: A manufacturing company's board has approved exploring a large-scale migration of 1,000 applications to AWS. The company has a small cloud team, no landing zone, no cloud governance model, and little migration experience. Before committing budget, executives want an objective assessment of the organization's preparedness across business, people, governance, platform, security, and operations, and a prioritized action plan to close the gaps. What should the solutions architect recommend FIRST?
o: Run an AWS Well-Architected Framework review in the AWS Well-Architected Tool for each of the 1,000 applications.
Start by rehosting the most business-critical application with AWS Application Migration Service so that the team learns by doing.
Produce a TCO business case with Migration Evaluator, and use the projected savings to determine readiness.

Conduct a Migration Readiness Assessment based on the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework perspectives, and use the results to build a plan that includes a landing zone, a cloud center of excellence, and skills training.

w.y: A Migration Readiness Assessment uses the six AWS Cloud Adoption Framework perspectives to measure organizational preparedness and produce a prioritized action plan. Doing this FIRST identifies gaps such as the landing zone, a cloud center of excellence and skills before large-scale migration starts.

o.A: Well-Architected reviews evaluate individual workloads, not organizational readiness, and 1,000 reviews is slow.
o.B: Starting with the most critical workload without governance or skills maximizes business risk.
o.C: A cost business case does not assess people, governance, security or operational readiness.
o.D: Correct: assesses organizational readiness across all six CAF perspectives.
